section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget's 4 Stages (Complete Sequence)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Arrange Piaget's four stages of cognitive development in the correct chronological order, from birth onward:

options.option_text: Sensorimotor → Pre-operational → Concrete Operational → Formal Operational
Pre-operational → Sensorimotor → Formal Operational → Concrete Operational
Formal Operational → Concrete Operational → Pre-operational → Sensorimotor
Concrete Operational → Formal Operational → Sensorimotor → Pre-operational

explanation: Piaget's four stages, in order: Sensorimotor (0-2 years, sensory/motor exploration, object permanence), Pre-operational (2-7 years, symbolic thought, egocentrism), Concrete Operational (7-11 years, logical thought on concrete objects), Formal Operational (11+ years, abstract/hypothetical reasoning).

section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget's 4 Stages (Complete Sequence)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A 9-year-old child who can conserve quantity and classify objects logically, but still cannot reason about a purely hypothetical scenario with no concrete referent, is in which Piagetian stage?
explanation: A 9-year-old with conservation and classification ability, but not yet abstract hypothetical reasoning, fits squarely in the Concrete Operational stage — logical operations are possible only on tangible, concrete content at this age.
